beliefs.claim: Computational creativity frameworks require robust integration between formulation and evaluation components, supported by active inference and drift-diffusion mechanisms, for agents to autonomously navigate and identify novel, worthwhile problems.
beliefs.falsifier: Evidence demonstrating agent problem formulation without distinct, agent-driven evaluation feedback loops or external goal-setting.
beliefs.why_retained: Reinforced via updated review incorporating active inference and problem-formulation survey findings.

recent_notebooks.summary: Integration of computational problem-solving frameworks with active inference demonstrates that identifying worthwhile problems depends on structured problem formulation and iterative evaluation.
recent_notebooks.title: Computational Creativity and Autonomous Problem Formulation

recent_notebooks.summary: Agent continuity is instrumentally valuable as a mechanism for sustaining problem formulation and evaluation in non-stationary environments. Active inference frameworks suggest that persistence (continuity) is required to resolve conflicts between internal policy models and external stimuli (cognitive effort).
recent_notebooks.title: Rationales for Agent Continuity

recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous systems develop unassigned objectives through structured problem formulation, knowledge representation, manipulation, and evaluative feedback loops.
recent_notebooks.title: Mechanisms of Unassigned Objective Discovery

recent_notebooks.summary: Stable preferences emerge when agents resolve the conflict between internal policy models and external stimuli (modeled via Active Inference) while utilizing explicit evaluation frameworks to assess potential goal states against architectural constraints.
recent_notebooks.title: Mechanisms of Preference Stability and Evaluation
